candidate.answerReason: Congruence is not guaranteed by general SSA data. B gives the intended SAS qualification: the included angle is required for applying SAS. Its word 'must' is not a universal necessity for congruence, since special nonincluded-angle cases such as HL also suffice.

methods.label: Distinguish SAS from SSA
methods.explanation: SAS requires the equal angles to be the included angles between the two sides. If the angles are opposite one of the sides (SSA), congruence is not guaranteed.
methods.levelReason: This is direct recognition of the Grade 8 SAS criterion and its included-angle condition.

review.mathematicalCheck: An equal included angle gives SAS; general SSA does not guarantee congruence. For example, an 8-unit side inclined at 30° has height 4, allowing a circle of radius 5 to meet the other ray twice and produce noncongruent triangles. B remains qualified as the intended SAS interpretation because its literal 'must' has exceptions such as HL.
